(a) the c-axis-shifts in HOPG depend strongly on the θ misfit, (b) the c-axis shifts in HOPGs with first-magic-angles of rotation are the highest, and (c) the c-axis shift is a direct consequence of symmetry enhancement at the magic angle.

(i) c-axis shifts in HOPG at the magic angle are anomalous, (ii) the c-axis shifts are strongly dependent on the misfit angle and (iii) additional symmetry elements appear in HOPGs with misfit angles close to the first magic angle.

(1) the c-axis shifts of HOPG depend strongly on the angle of rotation (θ) of the graphite layers, and are highest in proximity of θ misfit of ∼0.8°; and (2) the diffraction- peaks at ∼23 and ∼48 2θ vanish in HOPGs with a large misfit angle (θ misfit ≫1.5°).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the c-axis shifts in HOPG at the magic angle of rotations are anomalous in the sense that they are not only larger in comparison with the standard values of 0.0004 nm (at 300K), but also that the symmetry enhancement at the magic angle is not fully understood.
the c-axis shift is anisotropic and is a function of misfit angle.
the c-axis-shifts and symmetry enhancement observed in HOPG are due to the presence of magic angles of rotation, and that the first-magic angle corresponds to a θ misfit of ∼0.8°.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magic-angle in highly-oriented-pyroloic-graphite (HOGP) is not a simple twist, and the superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer-graphite (TBG) is not a trivial effect of the twist.
a new type of symmetry is introduced in the first-magic-angles of HOPG.

(i) a strong dependence of the c-axis shift on misfit-angle is demonstrated, and (ii) the diffraction peaks present in proximity of the magic angle are found to be associated with additional symmetry elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HOPG with θ misfit ∽1° is an ideal material for studying magic-angle-related phenomena, as the misfit angle and its associated symmetry elements can be tuned by controlling the temperature.
the c-axis-shift and diffraction peak intensity are strongly influenced by the misfit angle.
the symmetry enhancement is a general phenomenon in HOPG and is present for a wide range of θ misfit angles.
